about: OwnAudit category taxonomy (knowledge base). Maps each analyzer's ruleId
(exact, or a glob like `IDISP0*` / `*RESOURCE_LEAK`) to one of the problem
categories. aggregate/normalize.py reads this and labels every SARIF result.
Rules with NO mapping are NOT dropped - they land in `uncategorized` and are
surfaced in the coverage ledger, so the taxonomy grows deliberately instead of
Precedence: an exact ruleId match wins over a glob; among globs, the most
JSON, not YAML: OwnAudit's Python tooling is stdlib-only (CI installs no
packages), and the audit must not gain a PyYAML dependency to read its own
taxonomy. The mapping is a mechanical transcription of the YAML this was ported
from - the prose that lived in YAML comments moved into this `_doc` block, and
aggregate/tests/test_normalize.py can re-verify the transcription against the
reference file when a Own.NET checkout is present (OWNNET_REF).
OWN001: own-check OWN001 is an UMBRELLA leak code: one ruleId covers IDisposable
fields/locals, subscription tokens and timers, and the `[resource: ...]` tag in
the message text distinguishes them. A flat OWN001 -> category 1 would collapse
subscription/timer leaks (categories 2/3) into the IDisposable bucket and
undercount them, so normalize splits on the tag. The `*` arm is the fallback
(disposable / disposable field / pooled buffer, or no tag at all).
OWN014: Escape to a longer-lived region (vm -> App, SystemEvents) - NOT a generic
XAML: The XAML pass is a SECOND fact source, not a parallel linter: each rule maps to
one of the same categories so a markup finding rides the same fingerprint ->
baseline -> ratchet path as a .cs finding. Exact ids win over the `XAML1*` glob,
which is a safety net so a not-yet-mapped XAML rule never lands in
XAML203 is anchored at the code-behind subscription site so it lands at the same
file+line as own-check's OWN001 and CLUSTERS with it into one high-confidence
finding, rather than double-reporting on a separate .xaml line.
RUNTIME: correctness (category 5) - a storm in the same file as an INPC0xx hit clusters
with it into a high-confidence finding.
category_severity: Baseline P-level per category. Confidence (cross-tool agreement) is a SEPARATE
axis handled by scoring; this is severity only. Category 0 (uncategorized) is P3.
suppress: Third-party baseline-suppress. Findings whose path OR message contains one of
these tokens are third-party noise: dropped from the main report but COUNTED and
reported in the coverage ledger - nothing is hidden silently. This is an honest
third-party-namespace filter, not a regex heuristic over our own code.
coverage_notes: Analysis-skipped / coverage NOTES - diagnostics that are NOT verdicts. own-check
emits OWN050 ("cannot verify X - unresolved") when it cannot analyze something.
These must NOT be scored as findings: left in, they would show up as
uncategorized P3 candidates and add phantom pain. Instead they are routed to the
coverage ledger (analysis-skipped count) - the honest "we didn't see here".
